subject: Solaris AI renewal & capacity uplift — proposed terms
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@solarisaitech.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: Solaris AI annual renewal & capacity plan

Hi Lena / Rajiv —

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our conversation, I’m sending over an initial renewal proposal for your review. High level: 12‑month renewal starting 2027‑07‑01, baseline commit 120k tokens/month with an option to escalate to 150k/month during the first 90 days (billing adjusts to committed tier after ramp).

Attached: Solaris_SOW_v3.pdf (SOW with updated term and SLOs) and redwood_pricing_grid.xlsx (line item pricing and tier triggers).

Key asks from Solaris we captured:
- 20% uplift target for Q3 (you indicated possible increase as adoption grows)
- Procurement would like a short price guard while procurement processes the PO

We can accommodate a short price hold and bridge credit—I’ve looped Jordan (sales lead) and Markus (pricing) to finalize the numbers. Can you confirm the timeline Procurement needs for signatures? Also confirm whether the additional 30% sustained capacity would be required before or after go‑live for the new feature.

Next steps: I’ll follow up with a firm term sheet by Friday.

Best,
Camila
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Solaris_SOW_v3.pdf, redwood_pricing_grid.xlsx
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@solarisaitech.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@solarisaitech.com>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 11:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: Solaris AI annual renewal & capacity plan

Camila —

Thanks for the quick follow. A few items from Procurement and Engineering:

1) Price hold: Procurement wants a 90‑day price guard (no increases to per‑token list rate while PO in flight).
2) Bridge credits: Would be valuable to have a one‑time credit to offset overages during our ramp. We’re looking for something in the range of $25k–$40k.
3) Capacity: We expect to require a 20% bump immediately for a pilot feature rolling out in late July, with the potential to hit +40% by end of Q3. We need a clear upgrade path without multi‑week provisioning.
4) SLOs & penalties: Engineering wants clearer latency and availability SLOs in the SOW.

Can you share a firm term sheet and an editable SOW we can redline? Procurement is on a tight window — target signature by end of May if we can lock price.

Best,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Platform, Solaris AI
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: Solaris AI annual renewal & capacity plan

Camila / Markus —

Quick internal thread to align before we reply to Solaris. My read on concessions we can give without exec sign:
- Price hold: 90 days OK as long as the signature window is documented in HubSpot; prevents downstream churn.
- Bridge credit: we can offer a one‑time usage credit. We should aim mid‑range: $30k.
- Discount: suggest a 15% discount on current per‑token list for the 12‑month term (higher would need manager approval).
- Capacity uplift: guarantee rapid provisioning for the +20% pilot; anything above +30% for sustained load triggers a capacity review and priced commit step.

Two asks back to Solaris for this to work:
1) Commitment to a 12‑month term with a minimum baseline (120k tokens/month).
2) A ramp review after 60 days to confirm whether the uplift becomes permanent — that helps us scope reserved capacity vs burst.

Markus, confirm we can structure the bridge credit as a one‑time invoice credit (not prepaid) and that finance is OK with the 15% discount band for this AE.

Jordan
Director, Enterprise Sales

On Fri, May 14, 2027 at 08:35 AM Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Jordan — finance is OK with structure: $30k one‑time credit, 15% discount, 90‑day price guard.
> Need to add explicit ramp clause in SOW to govern provisioning timelines.
> —Markus
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@solarisaitech.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Solaris renewal — proposed commercial terms (v1)

Hi Lena / Rajiv —

Appreciate the clarity on procurement timelines. Per our internal alignment, please find the proposed commercial terms below. We’ve captured the SLO & ramp language in the attached SOW (Solaris_SOW_v3.pdf) and summarized the commercial items here for quick review.

Proposed terms (v1):
- Term: 12 months (2027‑07‑01 to 2028‑06‑30)
- Baseline commit: 120,000 tokens/month
- Capacity uplift: Guaranteed provisioning for +20% pilot within 5 business days of request. Sustained increases >30% will be discussed at ramp review and may require an amended commit.
- Pricing: 15% discount off current per‑token list rate for the 12‑month term.
- Bridge credit: One‑time usage credit of $30,000 applied to first two invoices.
- Price guard: 90‑day hold on list rate increases while PO is outstanding.
- Ramp review: 60 days after go‑live to validate usage and finalize commit adjustments.
- SLOs: 99.9% availability target, P95 latency targets included in SOW; remedies limited to SLA credits per SOW.

Attachments: Solaris_SOW_v3.pdf (editable, redline friendly) — please redline directly and return. I also included the redwood_pricing_grid.xlsx for clarity on tiers.

If this looks good, I can convert the SOW to a DocuSign packet and send the signature link. Procurement target of end‑May is feasible if we get a returned, signed SOW by 2027‑05‑25.

Best,
Camila

Attachments: Solaris_SOW_v3.pdf, redwood_pricing_grid.xlsx
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@solarisaitech.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@solarisaitech.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Solaris renewal — proposed commercial terms (v1)

Camila / Jordan / Markus —

Thanks — this is exactly the direction we needed. We accept the proposed terms with one small addition requested by Procurement: please add an optional 30‑day extension to the price guard if Solaris provides a PO within the 90‑day window but cannot complete signing due to internal signature routing (this extension must be documented in the HubSpot deal).

If you can add that clause to the DocuSign packet, we’ll route it through Procurement and Legal this week. Please send the DocuSign link when ready; Rajiv and I will review and sign.

Lena
